findings.title: AC-5's test never records the lite route it is given
quotes: Given a lite effort with its route recorded, when its spec.md is overwritten with the full refunds fixture
findings.fix: write spec-bugfix.md before `flow.start` (or start after drafting), then assert `lines_of(root)[0]["evidence"]["route"] == "lite"` before overwriting spec.md with the full fixture

sources.situation: in test_lite_escalated_to_full_runs_full_stages, `flow.start` runs before spec.md is written. `record` adds a route only when `header_route` finds one, and here spec.md does not exist yet, so the first history line carries no `route`. The test proves the escalation case for an effort with no recorded route. It does not prove it for one whose first line says `route: lite`, which is the precondition AC-5 states. The code reads only `== "full"`, so a recorded lite should not change the result, but the test does not show that.

findings.title: Route decision reads the history record without a change request against D-261028-4kji
findings.fix: record a change request (or a new decision that names D-261028-4kji) stating that the effort's route is taken from its first history line, and that this can only stop lite skips, never pass a stage

sources.situation: D-261028-4kji says an effort's stage is the first stage whose guards fail on its files, and that `nio flow done` "is not what makes a stage passed". It also records "Only `done` counts" as a rejected alternative. With this diff, the first history line, written by `nio flow start` or `done`, decides whether spec_jury, planning and plan_jury are skipped. A history line now changes which stages the derivation passes over, and no change request against D-261028-4kji records this exception.

findings.title: An effort started before spec.md exists never records its route
quotes: WHEN an effort's first history line is written (by `nio flow start` or its first `nio flow done`) THE SYSTEM SHALL record spec.md's route on that line.
if not lines and entries and (route := header_route(root, slug)):
findings.fix: record the route on the first line written once spec.md names one (e.g. when no line carries `route` yet), and have `ran_full` look for the first line that carries a route rather than only line 1.

sources.situation: `nio flow start` on an intake-only folder writes the first line with no route (spec.md is missing); every later line has history, so the route is never recorded. Until the spec jury has a round, rewriting that full effort's header to lite still silently skips spec_jury, planning and plan_jury, the bug of CB-1.

findings.title: A torn first write moves the route off the first line
findings.fix: put the route on the line after any repair insertion, or let `ran_full` scan for the first line carrying `route`.

sources.situation: the very first write crashes mid-line; the next write has no complete lines, puts `route` on its entry, then inserts the `repair` line before it. `ran_full` reads only the first line (the repair), so the recorded full route is ignored.

findings.title: A slugless `nio flow next` hides the route-changed refusal
quotes: return sorted(p.name for p in specs.iterdir() if p.is_dir() and kind(root, p.name) == "effort") if specs.is_dir() else []
`nio flow next` names the recorded and the header route
findings.fix: let `pick` consider `route changed:` folders too (they are efforts to report on), or have slugless `next` print route-changed efforts first.

sources.situation: the downgraded effort is the newest one; `nio flow next` with no slug picks from `efforts()`, which now excludes it, so it reports another effort (or none) and never names the two routes. The refusal shows only when the slug is given.
